resolver = "2"
exclude = ["experiments", "experiments-pro", "recovery", "legacy"]

serde_json = "1.0.149"
sha2 = "0.10.9"

# The project rule is safe Rust only. `deny` rather than `forbid` so the two host
# FFI seams (`view-abi`, `topcoat-js::collections`) and the backend's exported
# entry point can `#[allow]` it at the smallest scope.
[workspace.lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "deny"

# Dev builds optimise third-party code: the fixture-corpus tests spend a large share of their
# time in it (miniz_oxide inflate, object, postcard, serde_json; brotli and flate2 in the
# planner), and opt-level 2 runs them as fast as 3. Workspace members stay at opt-level 0,
# and so do the proc macros and everything under them: a package's profile is part of the
# identity of everything built on it, and the scripts hand rustc
# `target/debug/libjs_extern_macro.dylib` and `libjs_macro.dylib`, which must not change.
# `"*"` outranks `build-override`, hence the list: the registry packages that
# `cargo tree -e normal,build -p <macro>` prints for js-extern-macro, js-macro, serde_derive
# and thiserror-impl. Only `dev` is touched: the release backend dylib keys every sysroot.
[profile.dev.package."*"]
opt-level = 2

[profile.dev.package.proc-macro2]
opt-level = 0
[profile.dev.package.quote]
opt-level = 0
[profile.dev.package.syn]
opt-level = 0
[profile.dev.package.unicode-ident]
opt-level = 0
[profile.dev.package.serde_derive]
opt-level = 0
[profile.dev.package.thiserror-impl]
opt-level = 0
